claim: IL-1β is a master cytokine of local and systemic inflammation.
source: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) consists of two distinct forms (IL-1α and IL-1β) and is a master cytokine of local and systemic inflammation (Dinarello et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dinarello et al., 2012

claim: IL-1β is primarily produced by monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells in response to stimulation.
source: Primarily produced by monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells (DCs) in response to stimulation, IL-1β is involved in a variety of biological activities such as cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis through its binding to functional IL-1 receptor I (IL-1RI) expressed on virtually all cells.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction

claim: IL-1β binds to functional IL-1 receptor I (IL-1RI) expressed on virtually all cells.
source: Primarily produced by monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells (DCs) in response to stimulation, IL-1β is involved in a variety of biological activities such as cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis through its binding to functional IL-1 receptor I (IL-1RI) expressed on virtually all cells.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction

claim: IL-1β plays a role as a critical pathogenic mediator of many autoinflammatory, autoimmune, infectious, and degenerative diseases.
source: Thus, IL-1β plays a role as a critical pathogenic mediator of many autoinflammatory, autoimmune, infectious, and degenerative diseases (Dinarello, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dinarello, 2011

claim: IL-1β has been identified as an essential cytokine for Th17 differentiation in human T-cell immunity.
source: In human T-cell immunity, IL-1β has been identified as an essential cytokine with a role similar to that played by IL-6 in mice for Th17 differentiation, and is also important for expansion, in vivo survival, and effector function of IL-17-producing T cells (Acosta-Rodriguez et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Acosta-Rodriguez et al., 2007 and Lee et al., 2010

claim: IL-1β is important for expansion, in vivo survival, and effector function of IL-17-producing T cells.
source: In human T-cell immunity, IL-1β has been identified as an essential cytokine with a role similar to that played by IL-6 in mice for Th17 differentiation, and is also important for expansion, in vivo survival, and effector function of IL-17-producing T cells (Acosta-Rodriguez et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Acosta-Rodriguez et al., 2007 and Lee et al., 2010

claim: The IL-1RI knockout mouse is resistant to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis due to a failure to generate Th17 cells.
source: Even though TGF-β and IL-6 are sufficient for murine Th17 differentiation, the IL-1RI knockout (KO) mouse is resistant to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis due to a failure to generate Th17 cells (Sutton et al., 2006; Chung et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sutton et al., 2006 and Chung et al., 2009

claim: IL-1β, IL-23, and IL-6 are critical for generation of highly pathogenic Th17 cells in an autoimmune mouse model.
source: Further, IL-1β and IL-23 along with IL-6 are critical for generation of highly pathogenic Th17 cells in an autoimmune mouse model (Lee et al., 2012; Ronchi et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2012 and Ronchi et al., 2016

claim: IL-1β functions as a proinflammatory regulator of pathogenic human Th17 cells, which concomitantly produce IFN-γ and GM-CSF.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated that IL-1β functions as a proinflammatory regulator of pathogenic human Th17 cells, which concomitantly produce IFN-γ and GM-CSF (Zielinski et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zielinski et al., 2012

claim: The biological activity of IL-1β is tightly regulated at multiple levels by diverse mechanisms including receptor antagonism through production of a decoy receptor and soluble forms of signaling receptors or accessory proteins.
source: Due to its potent effect as a proinflammatory cytokine, the biological activity of IL-1β is tightly regulated at multiple levels by diverse mechanisms including receptor antagonism through production of a decoy receptor and soluble forms of signaling receptors or accessory proteins (Garlanda et al., 2013a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Garlanda et al., 2013a

claim: The IL-1R signaling complex includes the functional IL-1RI subunit and a signaling subunit, interleukin-1 receptor accessory protein (IL-1RAcP).
source: The IL-1R signaling complex includes the functional IL-1RI subunit and a signaling subunit, interleukin-1 receptor accessory protein (IL-1RAcP).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction

claim: Dimerization of the IL-1R1 and IL-1RAcP cytoplasmic Toll/IL-1R (TIR) domains initiates a signaling cascade through recruitment of adapter proteins.
source: Dimerization of the IL-1R1 and IL-1RAcP cytoplasmic Toll/IL-1R (TIR) domains initiates a signaling cascade through recruitment of adapter proteins (Garlanda et al., 2013b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Garlanda et al., 2013b

claim: The decoy IL-1RII has a short cytoplasmic tail lacking the signal-transducing TIR domain and acts as a molecular trap, capturing IL-1 with high-affinity and exerting a dominant-negative effect.
source: The decoy IL-1RII has a short cytoplasmic tail lacking the signal-transducing TIR domain and acts as a molecular trap, capturing IL-1 with high-affinity and exerting a dominant-negative effect (Shirakawa et al., 1987).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shirakawa et al., 1987

claim: IL-1RI is ubiquitously expressed, whereas the expression of IL-1RII is restricted to cells including monocytes, neutrophils, and B cells.
source: In contrast to ubiquitously expressed IL-1RI, the expression of IL-1RII is restricted to cells including monocytes, neutrophils, and B cells (Martin et al., 2017; Colotta et al., 1996; Colotta et al., 1993; McMahan et al., 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin et al., 2017; Colotta et al., 1996; Colotta et al., 1993; McMahan et al., 1991

claim: Human-activated Treg cells and follicular regulatory T (Tfr) cells upregulate IL-1RII to attenuate their IL-1-dependent responses.
source: In addition, it was recently demonstrated that human-activated Treg cells and follicular regulatory T (Tfr) cells upregulate IL-1RII to attenuate their IL-1-dependent responses (Tran et al., 2009; Ritvo et al., 2017), suggesting a physiological significance for IL-1RII expression in immune regulation.
evidence: Supported by citations to Tran et al., 2009 and Ritvo et al., 2017

claim: Deficiency of IL-1RII was found to exacerbate autoimmune arthritis by inhibiting IL-1 signaling in innate cells, such as macrophages and neutrophils.
source: Deficiency of IL-1RII was found to exacerbate autoimmune arthritis by inhibiting IL-1 signaling in innate cells, such as macrophages and neutrophils (Martin et al., 2017; Shimizu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin et al., 2017 and Shimizu et al., 2015

claim: IL-1RII mRNA expression is markedly higher in IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells compared to IL-1RI- memory CD4+ T cells.
source: Our previous study showed that IL-1RII mRNA expression is markedly higher in IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells compared to IL-1RI- memory CD4+ T cells.
evidence: Reference to authors' previous study

claim: Treatment with neutralizing IL-1RII antibody significantly augments IL-17 production by IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells in response to IL-1β and TCR stimulation.
source: Further, the negative regulatory role of IL-1RII was further evidenced by the significant augmentation of IL-17 production by IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells in response to IL-1β and TCR stimulation after treatment with neutralizing IL-1RII antibody (Lee et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2010

claim: Exogenous IL-1β treatment significantly increases the frequency of IL-17-producing cells in memory CD4+ T cells stimulated with anti-CD3/CD28.
source: The frequency of IL-17-producing cells and their level of IL-17 production were significantly increased by exogenous IL-1β treatment (Figure 1A and B) in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: IL-1β significantly enhances the frequency of IL-17/IFN-γ double producing cells.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Lee et al., 2012; Ronchi et al., 2016; Zielinski et al., 2012), IL-1β also significantly enhanced the frequency of IL-17/IFN-γ double producing cells, whereas IL-10-producing cells were decreased (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, and citations to Lee et al., 2012; Ronchi et al., 2016; Zielinski et al., 2012

claim: IL-1β treatment decreases IL-10-producing cells.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Lee et al., 2012; Ronchi et al., 2016; Zielinski et al., 2012), IL-1β also significantly enhanced the frequency of IL-17/IFN-γ double producing cells, whereas IL-10-producing cells were decreased (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: IL-1β treatment leads to upregulated expression of genes crucial for pathogenic functions of Th17 cells such as IL-22, Casp1, and several chemokines.
source: Furthermore, IL-1β treatment led to an upregulated expression of the genes which are crucial for pathogenic functions of Th17 cells such as IL-22, Casp1, and several chemokines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: The IL-17-promoting effect of IL-1β on human memory CD4+ T cells is not replaceable with IL-6 or IL-23.
source: The IL-17-promoting effect of IL-1β on human memory CD4+ T cells was not replaceable with IL-6 or IL-23 (Figure 1D), indicating the essential role of this cytokine for the Th17 response in memory CD4+ T cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D

claim: Th17 differentiation from naive CD4+ T cells is efficiently achieved in vitro by triggering the TCR in the presence of a mixture of Th17-polarizing cytokines.
source: In contrast to this, Th17 differentiation from naive CD4+ T cells was efficiently achieved in vitro by triggering the TCR in the presence of a mixture of Th17-polarizing cytokines, although IL-17 was minimally produced in the absence of IL-1β (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E

claim: IL-17 is minimally produced by naive CD4+ T cells in the absence of IL-1β.
source: In contrast to this, Th17 differentiation from naive CD4+ T cells was efficiently achieved in vitro by triggering the TCR in the presence of a mixture of Th17-polarizing cytokines, although IL-17 was minimally produced in the absence of IL-1β (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E

claim: Approximately 10% of ex vivo CD4+ T cells express IL-1RI.
source: Approximately 10% of ex vivo CD4+ T cells were found to express IL-1RI, whereas no obvious expression of IL-1RII was observed on the same cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: No obvious expression of IL-1RII is observed on ex vivo CD4+ T cells.
source: Approximately 10% of ex vivo CD4+ T cells were found to express IL-1RI, whereas no obvious expression of IL-1RII was observed on the same cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells have higher expression of IL-23R that is predominantly expressed in IL-17-producing cells.
source: These IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells also had higher expression of IL-23R that is predominantly expressed in IL-17-producing cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Wilson et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citation to Wilson et al., 2007

claim: IL-1RI-expressing CD4+ T cells are predominantly memory CD45RA-CD4+ T cells.
source: As reported (Lee et al., 2010), IL-1RI-expressing CD4+ T cells are predominantly memory CD45RA-CD4+ T cells (Figure 2B, p<0.001) and only a small fraction of naive CD4+ T cells express IL-1RI.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and citation to Lee et al., 2010

claim: Only a small fraction of naive CD4+ T cells express IL-1RI.
source: As reported (Lee et al., 2010), IL-1RI-expressing CD4+ T cells are predominantly memory CD45RA-CD4+ T cells (Figure 2B, p<0.001) and only a small fraction of naive CD4+ T cells express IL-1RI.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B

claim: TCR stimulation strongly triggers expression of both IL1RI and IL-1RII by memory CD4+ T cells, with rapid increase of their mRNA levels within 4 hr and sustained or even increased expression until 24 hr post-stimulation.
source: TCR stimulation strongly triggered expression of both IL1RI and IL-1RII by memory CD4+ T cells, with rapid increase of their mRNA levels within 4 hr and sustained or even increased expression until 24 hr post-stimulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A

claim: IL-1RI expression is significantly increased within 12 hr after TCR stimulation, whereas induction of IL-1RII mainly occurs in IL-1RI-expressing cells after 36 hr of stimulation.
source: Of interest, the kinetics of IL-1RI and IL-1RII expression differ noticeably in that IL-1RI expression is significantly increased within 12 hr after TCR stimulation, whereas induction of IL-1RII mainly occurs in IL-1RI-expressing cells after 36 hr of stimulation (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D

claim: IL-1RI expression is maximal even at the lowest concentration of CD3 Ab, whereas IL-1RII expression increases in a CD3 Ab concentration-dependent manner.
source: As seen in Figure 2E, IL-1RI expression was maximal even at the lowest concentration of CD3 Ab, whereas IL-1RII expression increased in a CD3 Ab concentration-dependent manner.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E

claim: TCR-stimulated memory CD4+ T cells can be subdivided into three subsets based on the expression of IL-1RI and IL-1RII: IL-1RI+IL-1RII-, IL-1RI+IL-1RII+, and IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells.
source: Our data show that TCR-stimulated memory CD4+ T cells can be subdivided into three subsets based on the expression of IL-1RI and IL-1RII: IL-1RI+IL-1RII-, IL-1RI+IL-1RII+, and IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C

claim: Around half of IL-1R+ memory CD4+ T cells co-expressed decoy IL-1RII on day 2 when expression of the two receptors peaked.
source: Around half of IL-1R+ memory CD4+ T cells co-expressed decoy IL-1RII on day 2 when expression of the two receptors peaked.
evidence: Stated as observation from experimental data

claim: No expression of IL-1RI or IL-1RII by naive CD4+ T cells occurs following TCR stimulation alone.
source: In stark contrast with memory CD4+ T cells, no expression of IL-1RI or IL-1RII by naive CD4+ T cells was found to occur following TCR stimulation alone.
evidence: Stated as observation from experimental data

claim: Th17-polarizing cytokines are required for induction of IL-1RI and IL-1RII by naive CD4+ T cells.
source: Rather, Th17-polarizing cytokines were required for induction of IL-1RI and IL-1RII by naive CD4+ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B

claim: Neutralizing antibody to IL-1RII significantly enhances the production of IL-17 by memory CD4+ T cells in response to TCR and IL-1β co-stimulation.
source: As seen in Figure 2F, neutralizing antibody (Ab) to IL-1RII significantly enhanced the production of IL-17 by memory CD4+ T cells in response to TCR and IL-1β co-stimulation.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F

claim: IL-1RII is preferentially expressed on TCR-stimulated Treg cells and is a useful selective surface marker of activated human Treg cells.
source: IL-1RII is preferentially expressed on TCR-stimulated Treg cells and thus, is a useful selective surface marker of activated human Treg cells (Tran et al., 2009; Mercer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Tran et al., 2009 and Mercer et al., 2010

claim: CD4+ T cells expressing GARP, a marker of activated Tregs, exhibit preferentially increased IL-1RII expression.
source: Similar to a recent report (Mercer et al., 2010), we found that CD4+ T cells expressing GARP, a marker of activated Tregs, exhibit preferentially increased IL-1RII expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and citation to Mercer et al., 2010

claim: A subset of IL-1RI+ CD4+ T cells without GARP expression also exhibits IL-1RII expression on cells in response to TCR stimulation.
source: However, a subset of IL-1RI+ CD4+ T cells without GARP expression also exhibited IL-1RII expression on cells in response to TCR stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B

claim: IL-1RII expression is not strictly limited to activated Treg cells.
source: Thus, this suggests that IL-1RII expression is not strictly limited by activated Treg cells.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations

claim: TCR triggering leads to the induction of IL-1RII expression even by Treg-depleted T cells.
source: TCR triggering led to the induction of IL-1RII expression even by Treg-depleted T cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A

claim: IL-1RII+ memory CD4+ T cells have higher expression of Foxp3 compared with the other two subsets.
source: Of note, these IL-1RII+ memory CD4+ T cells have higher expression of Foxp3 that could be induced in Treg-depleted conventional CD4+ T cells with Smad3- and NFAT-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 3) and other Treg-related markers such as CD39, CD73, and CTLA-4 (Figure 3B) compared with the other two subsets.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: IL-1RII+ memory CD4+ T cells have higher expression of Treg-related markers such as CD39, CD73, and CTLA-4 compared with the other two subsets.
source: Of note, these IL-1RII+ memory CD4+ T cells have higher expression of Foxp3 that could be induced in Treg-depleted conventional CD4+ T cells with Smad3- and NFAT-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 3) and other Treg-related markers such as CD39, CD73, and CTLA-4 (Figure 3B) compared with the other two subsets.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B

claim: Around 50% of IL-1RI+IL-1RII- and IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ cells have a Th17-associated phenotype (CD161+CCR6+).
source: As seen in Figure 3C, around 50% of IL-1RI+IL-1RII- and IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ had a Th17-associlated phenotype (CD161+CCR6+), whereas IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells mainly consist of Th1 (CD161-CXCR3+CCR6-) and non-Th1/17 subsets.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C

claim: IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells mainly consist of Th1 (CD161-CXCR3+CCR6-) and non-Th1/17 subsets.
source: As seen in Figure 3C, around 50% of IL-1RI+IL-1RII- and IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ had a Th17-associlated phenotype (CD161+CCR6+), whereas IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells mainly consist of Th1 (CD161-CXCR3+CCR6-) and non-Th1/17 subsets.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C

claim: A higher frequency of IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ cells show a phenotype typical of ex-Th17 cells (CD161+CXCR3+CCR6+).
source: Moreover, a higher frequency of IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ cells showed a phenotype typical of ex-Th17 cells (CD161+CXCR3+CCR6+), whereas the IL-1RI+IL-1RII- subset included more cells with the Th17 phenotype (CD161+CXCR3-CCR6+)(Basdeo et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated as observation from experimental data with citation to Basdeo et al., 2017

claim: The IL-1RI+IL-1RII- subset includes more cells with the Th17 phenotype (CD161+CXCR3-CCR6+).
source: Moreover, a higher frequency of IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ cells showed a phenotype typical of ex-Th17 cells (CD161+CXCR3+CCR6+), whereas the IL-1RI+IL-1RII- subset included more cells with the Th17 phenotype (CD161+CXCR3-CCR6+)(Basdeo et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated as observation from experimental data with citation to Basdeo et al., 2017

claim: IL-23R expression level is significantly higher in IL-1RI+IL-1RII- cells than IL-1RI+IL-1RII+, and IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells.
source: Although the frequency of IL-23R was comparable among three populations, its expression level was significantly higher in IL-1RI+IL-1RII- cells than IL-1RI+IL-1RII+, and IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4

claim: IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ cells consist of fewer IL-17-producing, but more IFN-γ-producing, cells than IL-1RI+IL-1RII- cells.
source: Intracellular cytokine staining (ICS) data revealed that IL-1RI+IL-1RII- and IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ cells had different cytokine production profiles, showing that IL-1RI+IL-1RII+ consists of fewer IL-17-producing, but more IFN-γ-producing, cells than IL-1RI+IL-1RII- cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D

claim: Cyclosporin A (CsA), an inhibitor of calcineurin, selectively represses the frequency of IL-1RII+ cells among TCR-induced IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: In preliminary experiments using inhibitors for TFs related to Treg cells, we found that cyclosporin A (CsA), an inhibitor of calcineurin, selectively represses the frequency of IL-1RII+ cells among TCR-induced IL-1RI+ memory CD4+ T cells in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B

claim: The immunosuppressive effect of CsA is mediated by inhibiting calcineurin-mediated dephosphorylation of the nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFATc).
source: The immunosuppressive effect of CsA is mediated by inhibiting calcineurin-mediated dephosphorylation of the nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFATc), which plays a critical role in peripheral activation and differentiation of Tregs (Kiani et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kiani et al., 2000

claim: Expression of IL-1RII mRNA is completely abrogated by treatment with CPP-conjugated VIVIT, a selective and potent inhibitor of calcineurin/NFAT interaction.
source: As seen in Figure 4C and D, expression of IL-1RII mRNA was completely abrogated and its protein level was also significantly diminished.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D

claim: IL-1RII protein level is significantly diminished by treatment with CPP-conjugated VIVIT.
source: As seen in Figure 4C and D, expression of IL-1RII mRNA was completely abrogated and its protein level was also significantly diminished.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D

claim: 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D3 [1,25(OH)2VD3] promotes Foxp3 expression in memory CD4+ T cells following TCR stimulation in the presence of IL-2.
source: Consistent with a previous report (Kang et al., 2012), 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D3 [1,25(OH)2VD3] promoted Foxp3 expression in memory CD4+ T cells following TCR stimulation in the presence of IL-2, and induction of Foxp3 was clearly attenuated by CsA treatment (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and citation to Kang et al., 2012

claim: Induction of Foxp3 is clearly attenuated by CsA treatment.
source: Consistent with a previous report (Kang et al., 2012), 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D3 [1,25(OH)2VD3] promoted Foxp3 expression in memory CD4+ T cells following TCR stimulation in the presence of IL-2, and induction of Foxp3 was clearly attenuated by CsA treatment (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E

claim: The expression of IL-1RII, but not IL-1RI, is significantly upregulated by treatment with 1,25(OH)2VD3 and IL-2 in memory CD4+ T cells at day 2 post-stimulation.
source: Moreover, the expression of IL-1RII, but not IL-1RI, was found to be significantly upregulated by treatment with 1,25(OH)2VD3 and IL-2 in memory CD4+ T cells at day 2 post-stimulation and resultantly, the ratio of IL-1RII+ to IL-1RI+ increased two fold (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F-H

claim: The ratio of IL-1RII+ to IL-1RI+ increases two fold by treatment with 1,25(OH)2VD3 and IL-2.
source: Moreover, the expression of IL-1RII, but not IL-1RI, was found to be significantly upregulated by treatment with 1,25(OH)2VD3 and IL-2 in memory CD4+ T cells at day 2 post-stimulation and resultantly, the ratio of IL-1RII+ to IL-1RI+ increased two fold (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F-H

claim: Foxp3 upregulation is associated with induction of IL-1RII.
source: This suggests that Foxp3 upregulation is associated with induction of IL-1RII.
evidence: Inferred from experimental observations

claim: NFAT and Foxp3 are essential for expression of IL-1RII by memory CD4+ T cells in humans.
source: Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that NFAT and Foxp3 are essential for expression of IL-1RII by memory CD4+ T cells in humans.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: Treg activity is modulated by a cooperative complex of NFAT and FOXP3.
source: It has been demonstrated that Treg activity is modulated by a cooperative complex of NFAT and FOXP3(27).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citation

claim: Peptide FOXP3 393–403 significantly inhibits IL-1RII expression by approximately 50% compared with the control peptide, FOXP3 399A.
source: Our data show that peptide FOXP3 393–403 significantly inhibits IL-1RII expression by approximately 50% compared with the control peptide, FOXP3 399A, (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C

claim: The NFAT/FOXP3 complex is important for IL-1RII expression.
source: Thus, this confirms the important role of the NFAT/FOXP3 complex in IL-1RII expression.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: Foxp3-Jurkat cells transfected with pGL4/IL-1RII-a1414 including the CNS region exhibit significantly higher luciferase activity compared with the other two constructs.
source: As seen in Figure 5D, Foxp3-Jurkat cells transfected with pGL4/IL-1RII-a1414 including the CNS region exhibited significantly higher luciferase activity compared with the other two constructs.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D

claim: Mutation of three bases within each NFAT binding site in the CNS region results in a significant decrease in IL-1RII promoter activity.
source: Mutation of three bases within each NFAT binding site in the CNS region resulted in a significant decrease in IL-1RII promoter activity (Figure 5D), indicating the importance of these sites for promoter function.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D

claim: NFAT recruitment to the DNA response element (NFAT B1: −1209 to −1188) in the CNS region of IL-1RII promoter is significantly enriched upon TCR stimulation.
source: NFAT recruitment to the DNA response element (NFAT B1: −1209 to −1188) in the CNS region of IL-1RII promoter was significantly enriched upon TCR stimulation, whereas Foxp3 was observed to bind a slight distant from the CNS region (Foxp3 B2: −425 to −418) of IL-1RII promoter (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and F

claim: Foxp3 binds a slight distant from the CNS region (Foxp3 B2: −425 to −418) of IL-1RII promoter.
source: NFAT recruitment to the DNA response element (NFAT B1: −1209 to −1188) in the CNS region of IL-1RII promoter was significantly enriched upon TCR stimulation, whereas Foxp3 was observed to bind a slight distant from the CNS region (Foxp3 B2: −425 to −418) of IL-1RII promoter (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and F

claim: NFAT recruitment to the B1 site is significantly enriched in Foxp3-expressing Jurkat cells upon stimulation with PMA and ionomycin compared with Jurkat cells without foxp3 expression.
source: NFAT recruitment to the B1 site were significantly enriched in Foxp3-expressing Jurkat cells upon stimulation with PMA and ionomycin compared with Jurkat cells without foxp3 expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3

claim: NFAT and Foxp3 bind directly to the IL-1RII promoter and regulate its transcription.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that NFAT and Foxp3 bind directly to the IL-1RII promoter and regulate its transcription.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: IL-1RI+ cells are the major IL-17 producing population regardless of IL-1RII expression following exposure to IL-1β.
source: Following exposure to IL-1β, IL-1RI+ cells were the major IL-17 producing population regardless of IL-1RII expression, whereas IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells predominantly produced IFN-γ (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and B

claim: IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells predominantly produce IFN-γ.
source: Following exposure to IL-1β, IL-1RI+ cells were the major IL-17 producing population regardless of IL-1RII expression, whereas IL-1RI-IL-1RII- cells predominantly produced IFN-γ (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and B

claim: IL-1RII expression attenuates the Th17 response of IL-1RI+ cells, as shown by a reduced frequency of IL-17-producing cells, and in particular IL-17 and IFN-γ dual producing cells.
source: IL-1RII expression, however, attenuated the Th17 response of IL-1RI+ cells, as shown by a reduced frequency of IL-17-producing cells, and in particular IL-17 and IFN-γ dual producing cells known as typical pathogenic Th17 cells (Figure 6A).
